question: Should Linux `system.notify` initially support only an argv-safe `notify-send` backend, or must the first implementation also include direct D-Bus or daemon-specific fallbacks?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but backend breadth determines dependency expectations, desktop-session behavior, security review scope, and whether this remains a focused node-host change.

options.title: Start with notify-send
options.body: Implement one documented `notify-send` backend with structured headless and missing-binary errors, leaving additional backends for evidence-driven follow-up.

options.title: Add D-Bus fallback now
options.body: Support both `notify-send` and direct freedesktop D-Bus delivery, accepting a larger implementation and test matrix for broader compatibility.

options.title: Defer to Linux app work
options.body: Leave headless Linux nodes unsupported and revisit notifications only through a future native Linux companion, despite `system.notify` remaining core-reserved.

recommendation.title: Start with notify-send
recommendation.body: Implement one documented `notify-send` backend with structured headless and missing-binary errors, leaving additional backends for evidence-driven follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail spans the node-host command architecture, CLI notification surface, policy, and core reservation involved in this choice.
